title: Evaluation of the Statistical Validity of Cervical Spine Measurements-Including Range of Motion, Strength, and Functional Test Results-for Return to Sport in Patients Who Have Undergone Surgery for Cervical Stenosis and/or Herniation.
official: Evaluation of the Statistical Validity of Cervical Spine Measurements-Including Range of Motion, Strength, and Functional Test Results-for Return to Sport in Patients Who Have Undergone Surgery for Cervical Stenosis and/or Herniation : Comparison Between a Group of Patients and a Group of Healthy Controls
summary: Cervical stenosis is characterized by a narrowing of the spinal canal that exerts pressure on adjacent sensitive areas, potentially causing significant neck pain and cervicobrachial neuralgia accompanied by functional limitations-conditions that are particularly disabling for athletes. Among the athletic population, anterior cervical discectomy with fusion is the gold-standard surgical treatment. Currently, there is no consensus regarding the timing for a safe return to sports following surgical treatment for cervical stenosis. While various clinical tests are used to assess mobility or pain, no single test specifically evaluates the level of functional recovery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patient group

Patients meeting all the following criteria will be included:

* Male or female aged 18 to 40 years
* Injury requiring surgery sustained during a sports activity
* Participation in sports activity at least once a week
* Cervical spine arthrodesis, cervical disc replacement, and/or foraminotomy
* Surgery performed by surgeons at the Centre Orthopédique Santy (Lyon)
* Inclusion based on the surgeon's decision during the 45-day post-operative visit

Control group

Participants meeting all the following criteria will be included:

* Male or female aged 18 to 40 years
* Participation in sports activity at least once a week
* No history of cervical pathology
* No history of surgery involving the shoulder girdle
* No neck pain in the month prior to the test

In both groups o Patient having signed an informed consent form Subject affiliated with or a beneficiary of a social security scheme

Exclusion Criteria:

Patient group

Patients meeting any of the following criteria will be excluded:

o Medical contraindication

Control group

Participants meeting any of the following criteria will be excluded:

* Reported history of spinal or upper-limb injury within the last 12 months
* Reported history of upper-limb surgery

In all cases, the following will be excluded:

* Protected individuals: adults under guardianship, curatorship, or other legal protection; individuals deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision
* Pregnant, breastfeeding, or recently delivered women
